PREMIERE316 STYLE-ONLY IMAGE REFERENCE CONTROL — V2
Asset ID: character-eve-first-woman-freed-appearance
Workflow profile: 4X3 (4:3)
Reference mode: ART DIRECTION ONLY — NO SUBJECT OR DESIGN TRANSFER.

The loaded images are non-content style plates. The asset prompt below is the sole authority for subject, identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, wardrobe design, prop design, environment geometry, creatures, crowd population, pose, action, camera composition, wounds, blood placement, text, and all story content.

ALLOWED TRANSFER ONLY: overall palette; contrast curve; key/fill/rim relationship; volumetric-light behavior; atmosphere density; material highlight and shadow response; lens/exposure language; practical texture fidelity; cinematic depth; restrained film grain.

FORBIDDEN TRANSFER: faces or facial geometry; body identity or proportions; hairstyles; costume silhouettes; wounds or blood maps; weapons or props; architecture or set geography; creature designs; crowd layout; pose; framing; four-panel layout; lettering; logos; or any recognizable object from a reference, unless the asset prompt itself explicitly requests that exact element.

Character guard: the row alone defines identity, age, ethnicity, anatomy, hair, scars, costume, wounds, pose, and carried objects. Never turn a non-Jesus character into a Jesus lookalike.

Active plate roles: warm-gold lighting and highlight rolloff; smoky umber shadow palette and ember atmosphere; abstract filmic tonal/material response and restrained grain; explicitly requested production-sheet spacing/readability only.
When a reference conflicts with the row prompt, ignore the reference and obey the row prompt.

AUTHORITATIVE ASSET PROMPT
--------------------------
EVE - FIRST WOMAN FREED — APPEARANCE: FOUR-VIEW IDENTITY, ANATOMY, COSTUME, AND CONTINUITY REFERENCE.

Create a four-view cinematic character ingredients sheet showing the same person in frontal three-quarter portrait, full-body, side profile, and rear-head/costume view. Lock facial identity, age, ethnicity, hairline, complete crown and rear hair, costume construction, body proportions, hands, scars, wounds, and carried props across every panel. One face exists only on the front of the head. Photorealistic live-action production reference, physically coherent lighting, exact anatomy, clean hands, consistent scale and materials, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no borders, and no written or graphical elements.

Cinematic biblical character ingredients portrait of Eve, the first woman freed from Hell, captured at the exact instant she stirs from millennia of sleep in Hell's inner prison chamber and recognizes her Redeemer. She is ancient beyond ordinary age yet fully human and alive—the mother of all living—appearing as a woman of immense age whose beauty has not been erased but translated into dignity, grace, and spiritual radiance. Approximate stature 5'4" to 5'6", slender and lightly built from endless captivity, bone structure delicate but strong: narrow shoulders, fine wrists, long fingers still capable of reaching. Skin is pale Mediterranean-to-Near-Eastern olive undertone washed nearly ashen by the cold of Hell, with thin translucent quality at temples and backs of hands; fine age lines at eyes, brow, and mouth; dust film and faint dried tear tracks on cheeks; subtle subsurface warmth returning where divine golden light first touches her face. No jewelry, no crown, no modern adornment.

Facial identity locked across all views: high soft cheekbones, gentle oval face slightly hollowed by time, straight refined nose, full but age-softened lips parted in awed recognition rather than fear, deeply set eyes of warm dark brown or deep amber-brown that catch divine light and ignite with impossible hope. Expression is the screenplay beat itself—awakening, recognition, profound relief and gratitude after endless waiting—not terror, not theatrical weeping alone, but luminous tears of joy gathering at the lower lids as she mouths or breathes the words of her line in spirit: "Our Redeemer..." Brows lightly raised; forehead softly lined; no makeup, no contemporary styling.

Hair is long pure white, the white of winter frost and ancient linen, cascading past the shoulders nearly to mid-back, with complete natural crown coverage and full rear hair mass always present. Fine texture with slight wave and weight; strands separate and catch rim light; a few wisps frame the face; no modern cut, no braids required unless a single simple age-worn plait at the nape appears in rear view only. Hairline natural and unbroken; never balding crown; never a second face or face-like form on the back of the head.

Costume is simple muted earth-tone linen garments consistent with ward-eve continuity: undyed and vegetable-earth palette of soft sand, dusty ochre, pale clay, and faded walnut-brown. Primary layer is a long ankle-length tunic or robe of handwoven linen with visible coarse-to-medium weave, thin from centuries of wear, frayed hem brushing bare or roughly sandaled feet, small tears at sleeve edges, dust and ash ground into the fabric folds. Optional light over-shawl or mantle of the same earth linen draped loosely over shoulders in some panels, never modern tailored. No embroidery logos, no metal ornaments, no contemporary fastenings—only simple cloth ties or natural fiber stitching. Fabric hangs with real gravity and soft translucency where backlit by divine gold; dirt maps and fold maps must lock identically across frontal, side, and rear costume views.

Hands are critical continuity: clean, anatomically correct, long-fingered, age-spotted, veins faintly visible, nails short and unadorned, slight tremor suggested in pose. In the hero emotional beat, both arms reach forward and slightly upward toward the off-frame presence of Jesus, palms open, fingers trembling and extended in longing and welcome—the first free gesture after chains. Broken or falling corroded iron chain links may rest near wrists or on the chamber floor as residual bondage just released, bloodstained and ancient, but she is no longer bound. No carried props beyond residual chain fragments if shown; she holds nothing else.

Four-view layout shows the same woman with locked identity: (1) frontal three-quarter portrait from mid-chest up, eyes alive with hope, white hair cascading, divine warm key light on face; (2) full-body standing or rising from kneeling captivity, linen robe full length, proportions and height clear, hands reaching; (3) pure side profile locking nose, brow, jaw, ear, and hair silhouette; (4) rear-head and full costume back view with complete crown and rear hair, garment construction, shoulder blades under thin linen, no face on the back of the head—only scalp, hair, and fabric. One face exists only on the front of the head in every panel.

Environment context is Hell's inner chamber at the liberation beat: vast dark stone prison atmosphere still lingering in cool blue torch light approximately 2000K at the edges, deep crimson and obsidian shadow in the deep background, while ethereal golden divine radiance approximately 6500K and warm amber fill enter from the shattered gate direction, painting her hair and cheekbones with living gold. Soft volumetric god rays cut through residual smoke and ash motes; dust hangs in the air; cold blue rim light on one side of her body contrasts warm amber key on the face—the color grade of warm amber against cold blue shadows that marks the transformation of the realm. No desert, no modern architecture, no readable inscriptions on walls.

Lighting and camera language for production reference: physically coherent multi-source light with clear key (divine gold from upper front-left or front), cool blue fill/rim from remaining hell torches, soft shadow under chin and within deep linen folds; subtle catchlights in both eyes; skin microtexture and linen fiber weave readable; shallow depth of field appropriate to character portrait panels without melting anatomy. Photoreal live-action biblical epic film still quality, as if photographed on a prestige period production—not illustration, not anime, not plastic CGI, not glamour studio beauty lighting. Aspect and framing serve a multi-panel ingredients sheet with consistent scale between panels.

Continuity locks repeated for model adherence: Eve is ancient first woman; long white hair with full crown and rear coverage; earth-tone worn linen only; pale aged Near-Eastern human skin returning to life under gold light; eyes of hope and recognition; reaching trembling hands; residual broken hell chains optional near wrists; warm amber versus cold blue grade; single human face only on the front of the head; identical facial structure, hairline, body proportions, hand anatomy, and garment construction across all four views. No modern objects, no eyeglasses, no logos, no watermarks, no captions, no borders, no written or graphical text elements, no celebrity likeness, no gore spectacle—reverent sacred biblical epic tone of liberation, maternal dignity, and first-woman hope fulfilled.
